issue.title: worker-executor.md: name the two trust stores and the Git rewrite that made the fan-out refuse
issue.body:
Two refusals cost time on the first Linux fan-out through the approved \`devin-local\` capability and neither is in \`docs/coder/worker-executor.md\`:

1. **Two Devin trust databases.** The worker runs with \`XDG_DATA_HOME=\$HOME/worker-jobs/xdg\`, so the Devin CLI's workspace trust lives there. A \`coder -p\` or \`coderbench run\` started from a shell without that variable consults the default store, where the checkout is untrusted, and the workspace probe answers \`present_unavailable\` (\`Refusing to run in an untrusted workspace\`). The fix is to run the terminal with the same \`XDG_DATA_HOME\` the worker uses, or to trust the checkout in both stores.
2. **A host-wide Git URL rewrite.** A global \`url.<x>.insteadOf\` makes CoderBench preflight see a rewritten origin and refuse the checkout (tracked separately as the preflight bug). Until that lands, \`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null\` on the CoderBench invocation is the workaround.

## What to do

Add a short troubleshooting section to \`docs/coder/worker-executor.md\` that names both refusals as they appear, says why each happens, and gives the fix, in the Google developer documentation style the repository uses (\`.agents/skills/google-developer-style/SKILL.md\`). Link the preflight issue for the second one rather than describing the fix to CoderBench itself.

## Acceptance

- The page tells an operator who sees either refusal what to do, without reading code.
- No secrets, home-directory paths beyond \`\$HOME\`-relative examples, or process environments in the page.
